sec.title: 1. Introduction
sec.p: Climate change is an omnipresent topic and affects every one of us. This is evident in the increasing and more intense occurrence of climate-related hazards, such as droughts and floods. Its effects will become more severe if no action is taken such as reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Therefore, the EU and its member states are taking various actions to reach their climate and energy targets. For this purpose, the European Council founded the European Environment Agency (EEA).

The EEA's goal is to contribute to the improvement of the environment in Europe and to support sustainable development. They aim to achieve this by providing timely, relevant, targeted and reliable information to the public and policy makers.

Since 2002, the EEA publishes an annual report “Trends and Projections in Europe” each year. The reports include an annual assessment of the EU's progress toward meeting its climate and energy targets. Since 2013, these reports have dealt with trends and projections in the three areas of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, renewable energy sources (RES) and energy efficiency (EE).

This review is based on all reports of the EEA from the year 2014 onwards. The aim of this review is to provide an overview of the current status by ensuring the long-term availability of detailed information from past reports. In the following, the three areas of GHG emissions, renewable energy and energy efficiency are explained in more detail. For each area, a short introduction, a tabular comparison, a corresponding figure and the main statements are given.

sec.title: 2. Greenhouse gas emission

list.list-item: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is one of the climate and energy targets. The EU committed to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 2010 to reduce its GHG emissions by 20% compared with 1990 levels by 2020. It also set further targets for 2030 and 2050. For 2030, the reduction target is a 40% reduction compared with 1990 levels and for 2050, the goal is to achieve an 80-95% emissions reduction and thus achieve climate neutrality.

sec.p: In July 2021, the European Commission proposed the "Fit for 55" policy package by stating that the reduction target should be increased from 40% to 55% by 2030, otherwise it will be difficult to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 [@R588059].

The figure "Historical trends and future projections for greenhouse gas emissions" shows the development of GHG emissions since 1990. The emission targets for the years 2020, 2030 and 2050 are highlighted. Furthermore, the future projections of two scenarios are shown. The with existing measures (WEM) future scenario reflects the effects of all adopted and implemented measures at the time the projections were prepared. The with additional measures (WAM) future scenario takes into account the additional effects of planned measures reported by Member States. Exact values can be taken from the table. For more detailed information, a detailed comparison is shown at the end of this review.

list.list-item: Target 2020: reduce its GHG emissions by 20% compared with 1990 levels
Target 2030: reduce its GHG emissions by 40% compared with 1990 levels (from the report 2021 the target is 55%)
*There are no values for these fields, as no values were collected for the WAM and WEM 2020 scenarios.
- The target will not be reached
+ The target will be reached

sec.p: Main statement Based on the figure, table and comparison we can observe the following statements:

list.list-item: According to the historical data, we have achieved the reduction target for 2020.
According to the current forecast, we will not be able to reach the reduction target for 2030 with the existing measures (WEM scenario).
According to the current forecast, we will not be able to reach the reduction target for 2030 *with the additional measures *(WAM scenario).
According to the current forecasts, we will probably not be able to reach the reduction target for 2050.

sec.title: 3. Renewable energy sources
sec.p: Another EU climate and energy target is that 20% of energy should come from renewable sources by 2020 and 32% by 2030. Renewable energy sources (RES) are used in the following sectors: power generation, heating and cooling and transport. For the transport sector, a 10% target must be achieved.

The figure “EU-27 shares of energy from renewable sources used by sector in the EU, 2005-2018 and proxy 2019” shows the development of the shares of renewable energies in the three sectors electricity, heating and cooling and transport.

list.list-item: Target electricity sector: 20% share of renewable energy in all energy consumed in electricity for 2020
Target heating and cooling sector: 20% share of renewable energy in all energy consumed in heating and cooling for 2020
Target transport sector: 10% share of renewable energy in all energy consumed in transport for 2020

sec.p: Main statement Based on the figure and comparison we can observe the following statements:

list.list-item: For 2020, the current forecast show that we are able to reach the goal for renewable energy use in sector electricity.
For 2020, the current forecast show that we are able to reach the goal for renewable energy use in sector heating and cooling.
For 2020, the current forecast show that we are not able to reach the goal for renewable energy use in sector transport

sec.title: 4. Energy Efficiency
sec.p: The last target deals with the topic of energy efficiency. Energy efficiency targets are expressed in primary and final energy consumption. Primary energy consumption measures the total energy demand of a country. It includes the consumption of the energy sector, losses during transformation, the distribution of energy and the final consumption by the end users. Final energy consumption includes energy supplies to industry, households, services, agriculture and transport. Supplies to the energy transportation sector and the energy industry are excluded. To meet the 2020 target requires a 20% reduction from projected 2020 levels, in primary or final energy consumption.

The figure “Primary and final energy consumption in the EU, 2005-2019, 2020 and 2030 targets and 2050 scenarios for reaching carbon neutrality” shows the development of primary and final energy consumption. The energy efficiency targets for the years 2020, 2030 and 2050 are highlighted. Furthermore, an indicative linear trajectory between 2005 and 2020 is plotted. This is used by the EEA to better monitor progress towards the energy efficiency targets. If the value of the current year is below the linear trajectory, then the energy efficiency targets are likely to be met. If not, then energy consumption must be reduced more rapidly to meet the targets. Exact values can be taken from the table. For more detailed information, a detailed comparison is shown at the end of this review.

list.list-item: Target 2020: reduction in primary and final energy consumption by 20 % compared with levels projected for 2020

sec.p: Main statement Based on the figure, table and comparison we can observe the following statements:

list.list-item: For 2020, the current forecast show that we are able to reach the goal for primary energy consumption (EU-27).
For 2020, the current forecast show that we are not able to reach the goal for primary energy consumption (EU-28).
For 2020, the current forecast show that we are able to reach the goal for final energy consumption (EU-27).
For 2020, the current forecast show that we are not able to reach the goal for final energy consumption (EU-28).
